text.p: Bonds closed well-supported but lost ground on the Bund and the Spanish bonos, with attention fixed on whether the Bank of Portugal will cut its money market rates on Wednesday.

The market, along with the rest of Europe, had been buoyed by European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy's remarks that the three percent of GDP budget criteria would not be brutally applied for entry to the single currency.
Few analysts expect the Bank of Portugal to make any cut but if it does, then the curve would be sure to steepen, with the period up to five years being the main beneficiaries, traders said.
"Tomorrow, we could see the spread narrow a little with the Bunds and move back to a discount with Spain," said one trader.
Traders said that if the Bank cut its 5.7 percent absorption rate or its 6.0 percent repo, then the spread with the Bund could close to around 60 basis points.

"After what Silguy said, the odds are clearly on the euro (single currency) starting in 1999. This gave support to the OT (Portuguese bonds). All that's missing is the Bank of Portugal," said another trader, referring to a possible rate cut.
